stages.title: Advanced vocabulary and terminology
stages.hook: Newspapers talk about 经济, 环境 and 科技. How can a few abstract words open up big topics?
explain: Advanced vocabulary is often made of abstract nouns and set collocations. 经济 (jīngjì, economy), 环境 (huánjìng, environment), 科技 (kējì, science and technology), 社会 (shèhuì, society) and 政策 (zhèngcè, policy) appear in news, essays and exams.

Many modern terms are built from familiar characters. 可持续 (kěchíxù) is "can continue", sustainable; 发展 (fāzhǎn) is development. Recognising the parts, such as 化 for -ize (现代化, modernisation) and 性 for -ness (重要性, importance), helps you decode new words.
Collocations matter: you 面临挑战 (face a challenge), 保护环境 (protect the environment) and 制定政策 (draw up a policy). Learn the verb with its noun.
stages.mnemonic: Learn words in pairs: 保护 + 环境, 面临 + 挑战.
sentences: The development of technology has changed society.
Protecting the environment is everyone's responsibility.

gq.q: Which verb goes naturally with 挑战?
gq.why: 面临 and 迎接 are common verbs with 挑战.

gq.q: What does the suffix 化 do in 现代化?
gq.why: 化 makes a verb or noun meaning "-ise" or "-isation".

panel.q: How can you guess the meaning of 可持续?
o: It must be memorised without clues
panel.why: It breaks down into 可 (can) and 持续 (continue).

panel.q: Why learn 保护环境 as a unit?
o: Because 保护 is a noun
Because it is a tone rule
Because 环境 is a verb
panel.why: Collocations show which words naturally go together.

panel.q: Which sentence is natural?
panel.why: 制定 goes with 政策.

teach.model: Many advanced words are abstract and built from familiar characters. Learn them with their typical verbs, such as 面临挑战. Suffixes like 化 and 性 help you decode new words.

points.ask: What should I learn with them?

trip.prompt: Read a Chinese news headline and find two abstract words.

stages.title: Academic language
stages.hook: In a research paper, you cannot say "I feel that…". Which words show evidence and logic?
explain: Academic Chinese uses a formal style. 研究 (yánjiū) research, 论文 (lùnwén) paper, 假设 (jiǎshè) hypothesis, 数据 (shùjù) data, 分析 (fēnxī) analysis and 结论 (jiélùn) conclusion are typical. Phrases like 研究表明 (research shows) and 综上所述 (in summary of the above) mark the argument.

Written academic style prefers two- and four-character forms and avoids spoken particles. It uses 本文 (this paper) instead of 我, and passive-like forms: 数据被收集 (the data were collected) or the 将 form: 本文将分析… (this paper will analyse…).
Citing sources (引用, yǐnyòng) is essential. Use phrases like 根据…的研究 (according to the research of…) and give notes. Do not copy, since academic honesty (学术诚信) is important in universities.
stages.mnemonic: 研究表明 opens the evidence; 综上所述 closes the argument.
sentences: Research shows that sleep affects learning.
This paper analyses the experimental data.

gq.q: Which phrase fits the end of an academic argument?
gq.why: 综上所述 sums up the evidence.
本文 is used in academic writing.

panel.q: Why does academic Chinese avoid spoken particles like 啊 or 吧?
o: Formal writing should be objective and precise
panel.why: Formal written style is objective and precise.

panel.q: A student copies a paragraph without a source. What is the problem?
panel.why: Copying without citing is plagiarism and breaks academic honesty.

panel.q: Which sentence is the better academic style?
o: 我觉得用的人越来越多啦
数据显示，使用率逐年上升
panel.why: It uses formal vocabulary and objective voice.

teach.model: Academic writing is formal and objective. It uses words such as 研究, 数据, 分析 and 结论, phrases such as 研究表明 and 综上所述, and it cites sources honestly.

trip.prompt: Read about citations and plagiarism and note one rule.

stages.title: Professional communication
stages.hook: You must write an email to a client and then run a meeting. What language does the office use?
explain: Workplace Chinese is polite and clear. 会议 (huìyì) means meeting, 日程 (rìchéng) schedule, 合同 (hétong) contract, 报告 (bàogào) report and 同事 (tóngshì) colleague. 截止日期 (jiézhǐ rìqī) is the deadline.

Requests are phrased politely: 请在周五之前提交报告 (please submit the report before Friday). Thanks use 感谢贵公司的支持 (we thank your company for its support), where 贵 (guì) is an honorific for "your". Use 敝公司 (bì gōngsī) for "our company" in humble speech.

Meetings follow a pattern: opening (开场), agenda (议程), discussion, summary and 跟进 (gēnjìn, follow-up). To disagree with a colleague, say 我有一点不同的想法 (I have a slightly different thought), which keeps harmony.
stages.mnemonic: 贵 for your side, 敝 for ours: honour them, humble us.
sentences: Please submit the report before Friday.
We have a meeting at three in the afternoon.
Thank you for your company's support.

gq.why: 贵 is an honorific meaning your.

gq.q: Which request is the most polite?
o: 请在周五之前提交报告
gq.why: 请 and 在…之前 is a polite, clear request.

panel.q: Why say 我有一点不同的想法 instead of 你错了?
panel.why: It disagrees without causing loss of face.

panel.q: What is the purpose of 跟进?
panel.why: It means to follow up on what was agreed.

panel.q: Which pair is a polite pair?
o: 敝公司 and 敝公司
贵公司 and 贵公司 for ours
贵公司 and 敝公司
你们公司 and 咱们公司
panel.why: 贵公司 for the other company and 敝公司 for our own.

teach.model: Workplace Chinese is polite and clear. Requests use 请 and a deadline. Honorific 贵 refers to the other party. After a meeting, people follow up with 跟进.

trip.prompt: Read about business etiquette in China and note one custom for meetings.

stages.title: Literary analysis
stages.hook: How can a single image, like the moon, carry feelings across centuries of Chinese writing?
explain: Literary analysis asks what a text says, how it says it, and why. 主题 (zhǔtí) is the theme, 人物 (rénwù) the characters, 情节 (qíngjié) the plot and 意境 (yìjìng) the atmosphere of a poem. 象征 (xiàngzhēng) means a symbol, and 比喻 (bǐyù) means a metaphor or simile.

In Chinese poetry the moon often symbolises longing for home, as in Li Bai's 静夜思. 对仗 (duìzhàng) is the parallelism of lines: in a couplet, words in the same position match in kind and meaning. Classical Chinese is very concise, and each character carries a lot of meaning.

Modern vernacular literature grew in the early 20th century. 鲁迅 (Lǔ Xùn) wrote 《狂人日记》 in 1918, one of the first modern short stories in vernacular Chinese. 《红楼梦》 by 曹雪芹 is one of the four great classical novels.
stages.mnemonic: Ask three things: what, how, why.
sentences: The theme of this poem is homesickness.
The author uses the moon to symbolise longing.

gq.q: What does the moon often symbolise in Chinese poetry?
gq.why: It often stands for longing for home or loved ones.
Cao Xueqin wrote the novel Dream of the Red Chamber.

panel.q: What does 对仗 mean in a couplet?
panel.why: Words in the same position match in kind and meaning.

panel.q: Why is 《狂人日记》 important?
o: It was an early modern vernacular story
panel.why: It was one of the first modern short stories in vernacular Chinese.

panel.q: A student says a poem about the moon is only about astronomy. What is a better analysis?
o: The moon is only a place
panel.why: Literary analysis looks at symbolism as well as literal meaning.

teach.model: To analyse a text, look at theme, characters, plot and symbols. In Chinese poetry the moon often stands for longing. Couplets use parallelism, and modern vernacular literature began in the early 20th century.

trip.prompt: Read the summary of Dream of the Red Chamber and note its main theme.

stages.title: Advanced listening comprehension
stages.hook: A speaker says 这个方案还不错 with a flat tone. Do they really mean it is good? Listening between the lines matters.
explain: Advanced listening means more than words. 语气 (yǔqì, tone of voice or mood) shows attitude. A phrase like 还不错 (not bad) is mild praise, and 还行 means so-so. 言外之意 (yánwàizhīyì) is the meaning beyond the words, such as hearing "I'm busy" as a polite refusal.

Lectures (讲座, jiǎngzuò) and interviews (采访, cǎifǎng) have signals: transition words such as 但是, 不过 and 然而 (however) mark a turn (转折, zhuǎnzhé). Take notes (记笔记) by writing key words only, and listen for numbers, lists and conclusions.
Chinese speakers may use indirect language to be polite. 我再考虑一下 (I'll think about it) can mean no. Listening for what is left unsaid, and watching tone, helps avoid misunderstanding.
stages.mnemonic: Listen to the words, then to what hides behind them.
sentences: His words have a hidden meaning.
Take notes when you listen to a lecture.
Pay attention to tone and turns.

gq.q: What does 还不错 usually express?
Which word signals a turn in an argument?

panel.q: A colleague says 我再考虑一下 in a hesitant tone. What might it mean?
panel.why: It can be a polite way to say no.

panel.q: What should you write when taking notes during a lecture?
panel.why: Key words, numbers and conclusions are efficient.

panel.q: What is 言外之意?
panel.why: It is meaning that is implied beyond the literal words.

teach.model: Listen to the words and also to the speaker's mood. Phrases like 还不错 are mild. 言外之意 is meaning beyond the words. In lectures, watch for turn words like 然而 and take notes of key words.

points.ask: What else do I listen to?

trip.prompt: Read about implicature and give one example.

stages.title: Oral fluency and presentations
stages.hook: A fluent speaker sounds natural not because they speak fast, but because of rhythm and pauses. Try it.
explain: Fluency (流利, liúlì) in Mandarin depends on rhythm (节奏, jiézòu), pauses (停顿, tíngdùn) and intonation (语调, yǔdiào). Stress is placed on meaningful words, and the neutral tone gives a light beat to grammatical words. Do not pause in the middle of a word, but between phrases.

In presentations, use transitions (过渡): 接下来 (next), 换句话说 (in other words), 比如 (for example). Emphasise a key point with 重要的是… (the important thing is…) or 关键在于… (the key lies in…). Finish with a summary and an invitation: 现在欢迎大家提问 (now questions are welcome).
Prepare, but avoid reading a script. Practise with a timer, record yourself and check the tones of the key words. If you make an error, correct it calmly and continue.
sentences: Please pay attention to intonation and pauses.
Now everyone is welcome to ask questions.

o: In the middle of a word
gq.why: Pause between phrases, not inside words.

panel.q: A speaker talks very fast but pauses in the middle of words. What should they improve?
panel.why: Rhythm and pauses matter more than speed.

panel.q: Why do presenters use 接下来?
panel.why: It signals a transition to the next point.

panel.q: What is a good practice habit?
panel.why: Recording yourself lets you check tones and rhythm.

teach.model: Fluency is about rhythm, pauses and intonation, not only speed. Use transition words like 接下来 and emphasis phrases like 重要的是. Practise by recording yourself.

points.ask: How do I move between points?

trip.prompt: Read about intonation and compare it with tone in Mandarin.

stages.title: Translation and interpretation
stages.hook: A conference interpreter speaks while the speaker is still talking. How is that possible?
explain: Translation and interpretation are different. 笔译 (bǐyì) is written translation and 口译 (kǒuyì) is oral interpretation. 同声传译 (tóngshēng chuányì) is simultaneous interpreting, done almost at the same time with headphones. 交替传译 (jiāotì chuányì) is consecutive: the speaker pauses, then the interpreter speaks.

In 1898 Yan Fu (严复) proposed three standards of translation: 信 (xìn, faithful), 达 (dá, expressive and clear) and 雅 (yǎ, elegant). Today people still discuss them. 术语 (shùyǔ, terminology) must be consistent, and 译员 (yìyuán) must be neutral and accurate.

Interpreters manage memory and decide quickly. They compress long sentences, handle names and numbers carefully, and keep the speaker's tone. Mistranslations (误译) can cause real problems, for example in contracts or medicine.
sentences: The translator must be faithful to the original.
A good translation needs faithfulness, clarity and elegance.

gq.why: 同声传译 is done almost at the same time as the speaker.

gq.q: What does 信 in 信达雅 mean?
gq.why: 信 means faithful to the original.

panel.q: How does consecutive interpreting work?
o: The interpreter writes it down only
panel.why: The speaker pauses and the interpreter then speaks.

panel.q: Why must terminology be consistent in a contract translation?
o: Different terms can change the meaning
panel.why: Different terms for the same concept could change legal meaning.

panel.q: An interpreter changes a number from 15 to 50 by mistake. What kind of problem is this?
panel.why: Numbers are crucial, and an error is a serious mistranslation.

teach.model: Translation is written and interpreting is spoken. Simultaneous interpreting is almost live, and consecutive waits for the speaker to pause. Yan Fu's 信达雅 sets three standards: faithful, clear and elegant.

points.ask: What are the two interpreting modes?

trip.prompt: Read about Yan Fu and find his three standards.

stages.title: Idiomatic and figurative language
stages.hook: "Draw a dragon and dot its eyes." What would this idiom mean in a speech or an essay?
explain: Chengyu (成语) are four-character set phrases, often from classical stories. 画龙点睛 (huà lóng diǎn jīng) means to add the finishing touch that brings a thing to life. 守株待兔 (shǒu zhū dài tù) is to wait by a tree stump for a rabbit, meaning to wait for luck instead of acting.

亡羊补牢 (wáng yáng bǔ láo) means to mend the pen after a sheep is lost: it is not too late to fix a mistake. 井底之蛙 (jǐng dǐ zhī wā) is a frog at the bottom of a well, a person of narrow view. 一举两得 means to gain two things at once, and 半途而废 means to give up halfway.

Chengyu should be used with their exact meaning and their fixed form. 对牛弹琴 (playing a lute to a cow) means to speak to someone who cannot understand. 塞翁失马 (the old man lost a horse) teaches that a misfortune may turn out to be a blessing. Do not translate them word for word.
stages.mnemonic: Each chengyu hides a tiny story.
items: wait for luck by a stump
mend the pen after losing sheep
kill two birds with one stone
speak to someone who cannot understand
sentences: His words were the finishing touch.
Do not wait for luck, you must act.
Mending the pen after losing sheep is not too late.

gq.q: Which chengyu advises that it is not too late to fix a mistake?
gq.why: 亡羊补牢 means to repair after loss.

gq.q: Which chengyu describes someone with a narrow view?
gq.why: 井底之蛙 sees only a small piece of sky.

panel.q: A student gives up after one week of practice. Which chengyu fits?
panel.why: 半途而废 means giving up halfway.

panel.q: Why should chengyu not be translated word for word?
o: The meaning comes from the story
panel.why: Their meaning comes from the story, not the literal words.

panel.q: Explaining grammar to a person who does not know the language is like which idiom?
panel.why: 对牛弹琴 means speaking to someone who cannot understand.

teach.model: Chengyu are four-character sayings, each with a story. 画龙点睛 is a finishing touch, 守株待兔 is waiting for luck, and 亡羊补牢 is fixing a mistake. Use them with their set form and exact meaning.

points.ask: Where does the meaning come from?

trip.prompt: Pick a chengyu from the page and read the story behind it.

stages.title: Extended independent writing
stages.hook: You are asked to write 500 characters arguing for a view. How do you plan an essay that convinces?
explain: An argumentative essay (议论文, yìlùnwén) has a clear 论点 (lùndiǎn, thesis), 论据 (evidence) and 论证 (lùnzhèng, reasoning). The opening (开头) should attract the reader and state the thesis, the body develops reasons with examples and the ending (结尾) restates the conclusion.

Use transition sentences (过渡句) so that paragraphs connect. Vary the sentence length, and use a few chengyu or quotations if they fit, but do not overuse them. Use 因此, 然而 and 由此可见 (thus it can be seen) to show logic.

Revising (修改, xiūgǎi) is part of writing. Check the thesis, the order of ideas, character accuracy, 的/得/地, punctuation and tone of voice. Reading aloud helps you find awkward phrases. Good style (文笔, wénbǐ) comes from clarity first.
stages.mnemonic: Thesis, evidence, reasoning; then revise, revise.
sentences: A good essay needs a clear thesis.
The opening should attract the reader.

gq.why: It is the main claim of an essay.
The ending 结尾 sums up the thesis.

panel.q: Which expression shows logical consequence?
panel.why: 由此可见 means thus it can be seen.

panel.q: Why read your essay aloud?
panel.why: It helps you notice awkward phrases and rhythm.

panel.q: A student uses a chengyu in every sentence. What is the better advice?
o: Use a few that fit well
panel.why: Too many idioms make writing stiff; use a few that truly fit.

teach.model: A good argumentative essay has a clear thesis, evidence and reasoning. The opening attracts, the body develops reasons, and the ending sums up. Revise for logic, characters and punctuation.

points.ask: What does an essay start with?
What do I do at the end?

trip.prompt: Read about essay structure and compare with a Chinese essay plan.
